transcript.text: quick q: churn with 3% positives, should i report PR-AUC or ROC-AUC to my manager, and why? no data work, just the answer

**Report PR-AUC as your headline number, and give ROC-AUC as a secondary one.**

**Why PR-AUC**
- With 3% positives, ROC-AUC can look good even when the model is poor for the retention team. Its false-positive rate divides by the huge pool of non-churners. A model can raise many false alarms and still post a high ROC-AUC. - PR-AUC tracks what your manager cares about: of the customers we flag, how many really churn (precision), and how many of the churners we catch (recall). - The baseline is clear. **Caveats**
- PR-AUC depends on the churn rate. Don't compare it across segments or periods with different rates unless you also show the baseline. - ROC-AUC is still useful as a measure of ranking quality that doesn't depend on the churn rate. Keep it as a supporting number. **What to add for a manager**
A single AUC rarely drives a decision. Add one line at the operating point your team can act on. For example: "If we contact the top N% by risk, we catch X% of churners, and Y% of those contacted would have churned." Pick N from the retention team's capacity. Compute all of these on a holdout set the model never saw, ideally split by time.
